fatal_errors: The proposed FCC high-entropy alloy does not identify the target BCC NbMoTaWRe film.
It replaces Re alloying and He2+ implantation with unspecified compositional tuning and heat treatment.
It addresses generic tensile ductility rather than irradiation hardening, helium-bubble segregation, and grain-boundary embrittlement.
The proposed slip and grain-boundary-sliding mechanism does not match the target defect-sink and helium-bubble-suppression mechanism.
No supporting evidence is cited, and the alloy composition, heat treatment, and baseline are insufficiently specified.
explanation: The hypothesis is a generic proposition that FCC-rich alloys can be ductile, but it does not reconstruct the target result: Re-containing, single-BCC NbMoTaWRe sputtered films showed improved room-temperature helium-irradiation resistance relative to Re-free NbMoTaW. The relevant explanation is that Re-induced grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, and amorphous grain-boundary regions provide defect sinks that suppress helium-bubble growth and boundary segregation, thereby reducing irradiation hardening and embrittlement. Room temperature is the only meaningful condition overlap. The paired tensile experiment could test the generic FCC claim, but undefined processing and composition plus an arbitrary 20% threshold limit discriminability and do not test the hidden target.
